What changed and why:

**`PrefixCalculator.java`** — `@FunctionalInterface` with three built-in strategies as static factory methods, following the `Comparator` idiom:
- `iterative()` — the original loop, O(n) sequential.
- `recursive()` — uses a `private static` helper (Java 9+) to accumulate in-place; demonstrates the pattern accepts any algorithm.
- `parallel()` — delegates to `Arrays.parallelPrefix`, which uses a fork/join tree reduction; worth having for large arrays on multi-core hardware.

**`PrefixSum.java`** — all calculation logic is removed from the class itself. The constructor now just validates inputs and calls `calculator.calculate(arr)`. Two `of` overloads: the zero-argument one defaults to `iterative()` so existing callers are unaffected; the second accepts any `PrefixCalculator`, including lambdas the caller writes themselves.
